Social posts, the Google Business Profile, reviews, the website and AI search all send renters signals about the same community. When different vendors run each piece, the details drift apart: one set of photos on Google, another on the website, and hours that never quite match. The SocialDM brings those pieces into one system, so a renter sees the same story wherever they look.

Read how The SocialDM brings apartment SEO, Google Business Profile optimization, social media and paid media into one unified system.

info.text:
A lease up opens with no search history.
That's the part most launch plans skip.

No reviews yet. Few photos. No track record for Google or an AI assistant to point to. The building is ready long before its online presence is.

What tends to help in the first 90 days:

• A complete Google listing on day one, with real photos as soon as homes are ready
• Answers to the questions renters ask most, written on the website
• A reply to every early review
• The same details everywhere a renter looks

The communities that start early don't have to catch up later.

A modern building, a clear sky and a renter wondering what life is like inside. The best apartment pages answer that before anyone has to ask.

Before a tour, renters want the practical details: which floor plans fit, what amenities are really there, whether pets are welcome and what a current concession looks like. Pages that answer those questions in plain words help a community show up when renters compare options on Google, Google Maps and AI platforms, and they keep the click from going to a listing site first.

info.text:
Posting more is not a strategy.
Posting what renters ask about is.

A full calendar of "Happy Monday" posts and stock sunsets looks busy. It rarely fills a tour schedule.

The posts that pull their weight answer something: what is included, what the neighborhood is like, which homes are available, what the team is like to work with. They match the website and the Google listing, and they change with the season.

Frequency still matters. It just comes second.

info.text:
In March, a new 183 home community outside Portland appeared in Google search and maps about 970 times. By September, it was close to 2,900.

Some of that is a lease up finding its feet. A big part, in our view, is how much more Google could find, trust and show about it: details that match everywhere, fresh photos and posts, and a reply to every review.
